subject: Business
title: Fractional Reserve Banking
description: A fast breakdown of Fractional Reserve Banking for builders.

hook.text: You deposit $1,000. The bank lends $900 to someone else. That person deposits it. The bank lends $810. Money multiplies.

buildup.text: Fractional reserve banking means banks keep a fraction of deposits and lend the rest.

discovery.text: This process creates money. A single $1,000 deposit can generate $10,000 in total bank deposits.

twist.text: If everyone withdraws at once, the bank can't pay. That's a bank run — and it's happened hundreds of times.

climax.text: Deposit insurance (FDIC) was created after the 1930s bank runs to prevent panics. It mostly works.

punchline.text: Banks create money from thin air. Insurance keeps us from noticing.

quiz.question: How does fractional reserve banking create money?
options: Banks lend most deposits, which get redeposited and re-lent, multiplying the original amount
Banks print physical currency in their vaults
The government gives banks extra money every month

details.summary: Fractional reserve banking allows banks to lend out most of their deposits while keeping only a fraction in reserve. This system effectively multiplies the money supply because deposits create loans that become new deposits in other banks, expanding credit throughout the economy.
details.whyItMatters: This system is how most money in the economy is actually created, not by printing but by lending. Understanding fractional reserves reveals both the engine of economic growth and the vulnerability that causes bank runs and financial crises.
takeaways: Banks keep only a small fraction of deposits as reserves and lend the rest
Each loan creates new deposits multiplying money through the banking system
Bank runs occur when too many depositors demand cash simultaneously

faq.question: How does fractional reserve banking create money?
faq.answer: You deposit 1,000 dollars. The bank keeps 100 in reserves and lends 900. The borrower spends it and the recipient deposits 900 in their bank. That bank keeps 90 and lends 810. This chain continues, ultimately creating several thousand dollars from your original 1,000.

faq.question: What happens when too many people withdraw at once?
faq.answer: A bank run occurs because the bank does not hold enough cash for all depositors simultaneously. Government deposit insurance like FDIC prevents most modern bank runs by guaranteeing deposits up to 250,000 dollars, maintaining public confidence in the banking system.
